newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: U.N. agency airlifts food to Angola's displaced.
newsitem.headline: U.N. agency airlifts food to Angola's displaced.

text.p: The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) said on Wednesday it had airlifted 40 tonnes of emergency supplies to Angola's northwest region to feed growing numbers of people displaced by fighting.

The WFP said in a statement more than 6,000 displaced people have sought refuge in the government-held town of N'Zaji in Lunda Norte province from outlying villages since late May with over 1,000 people arriving in the last two weeks.
"Reports indicate that hundreds more people are on the way," the WFP said, adding that nearly 60 percent of the displaced population were women, children and elderly people.
The Angolan government and the former rebel UNITA movement signed a peace treaty in 1994 to end two decades of civil war and agreed to merge their armies and create a single national army.

But the government has accused UNITA of still having several thousand soldiers in the countryside, even though the movement declared at the end of last year it had dismantled its entire guerrilla force under U.N. supervision.
In May, the Angolan armed forces began an offensive in UNITA-held diamond areas in the northeast, which it said was aimed at rooting out armed refugees from the former Zaire.
But Western diplomats have said this was just a pretext by the government to extend its control over the country.

The WFP said missions undertaken this month by its workers as well as the U.N. children's fund and Lutheran World Federation had spotted groups of displaced people south of N'Zaji in the areas of Cossa, Maludi and M'Buia.
They were walking towards N'Zaji where they were expected to arrive within days.
Other groups told aid workers they had recently emerged from the bush after hiding for as long as three weeks with little access to food and assistance.

Since June, the WFP has delivered 107 tonnes of relief food packages at a cost of $37,450 to the area. It has also donated seven tonnes of clothing and 500 survival kits purchased from the UNHCR refugee agency.
